prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: ONE original mobile virtual-pet character concept sheet for art-direction review, landscape, three equally sized columns A B C on a quiet warm ivory background.
Primary request: Design three genuinely appealing original collectible pet characters for an adult/college-age cozy mobile pet-care game. They must feel authored by a skilled game character artist, with nuanced silhouette, expressive resting pose, clear shape hierarchy, usable hands/paws for feeding, and clothing potential. This is a still concept study, not a game screenshot or animation asset.
All three are polished 2D game illustration with restrained dimensional shading, confident organic contours, very subtle paper texture, warm natural colors, small readable eyes and delicate characterful details. No glossy plastic, no photoreal fur, no 3D clay, no human body, no generic capsule dolls, no monkey or humanoid doll, no oval hooded baby in an animal costume. Do not imitate an existing franchise.
Column A: an inviting compact honey-and-cream puppy, low seated pear silhouette with anatomical shoulder and haunch transitions, wide soft cheek head, one folded ear and one relaxed ear, front paws with a distinct wrist resting near its belly, tiny belly tuft, approachable gentle curiosity. A small properly constructed moss-green vest with separate collar, armholes, seams and hem, not an oval patch.
Column B: a mischievous warm-grey and ivory cat, taller springy angular-but-soft silhouette, offset tucked paw and naturally curved tail, broad brow and small triangular ears, slight curious lean. A short rust-red chore jacket with sleeves, collar and two pocket shapes; leave clear negative space between arm and torso. Distinct silhouette and attitude from A.
Column C: an affectionate cream lop-eared rabbit, very compact seated bean-shaped haunches but with distinct foot/paw structure, long asymmetrical drooping ears framing its face, calm sleepy tilt, small forepaws ready to cradle food. A soft blue bib-overall with real straps, small chest pocket and readable leg openings. Clearly a rabbit, not a person in a bunny costume.
Composition: one large full-body frontal or near-frontal character per column, all fully in frame, same apparent character height, spare ground contact shadow, no scenery or interface. Below each large character show one much smaller exploratory gesture of that SAME character leaning forward with both paws reaching to receive a small biscuit; consistent art and design.
Faces: draw simple original ANIMAL facial features for this body-and-style concept study only. No real-person or synthetic-human face, no face-swapped photo, no blank uncanny masks. Keep broad near-frontal face areas that can be evaluated for photo compositing in a subsequent separate test. Do not pretend a real person's identity is being preserved.
Text: only the three small labels "A", "B", "C" above respective columns, no other text.
Priority: beautiful finished character shapes, pose appeal, thoughtfully fitted actual clothing, clear differences between candidates. Illustration beauty and animation-ready structure both matter.
